newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Lyonnais shares slip on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Credit Lyonnais shares slip on profit-taking.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais investment certificates were down sharply in morning trade as investors took profits following its run-up in recent weeks.

The investment certificates in the state-controlled bank make up around a fifth of its capital but carry no voting rights and are seen as a speculative play. They were down 6.47 percent at 130.0 francs by 0900 GMT on volume of 14,028.
"They've been climbing a lot in recent days," one analyst said. "Also the fact that (Groupe) Paribas has said it isn't interested in buying it may have taken the steam out of them."

The European Commission approved on Wednesday a 3.9 billion franc French government emergency aid package for the bank that will waive much of the burden imposed on the bank by last year's rescue package.
The bank now is expected to post a profit at the half-year stage whereas previously it was expected to announce a loss.
The government has said that a third bailout on top of the emergency aid will be needed to get the bank in shape for privatisation but has said it is open to any offers as of now.
